correctness.rationale: Each two-level positive matrix has powers affine in spectral projections P,Q. The canonical two-projection decomposition gives orthogonal one- and two-dimensional reducing principal-angle blocks. The published fully general n=2 weak singular-value majorization for crossed versus ordinary Heinz expressions applies on each 2-block, equality on 1-block, and Ky Fan partial sums are subadditive under concatenation. Thus s(C_t) is weakly majorized by s(H_t) for arbitrary n and independently chosen spectral levels. Trace expansion leaves precisely alpha_t alpha_{1-t} beta_t beta_{1-t} Tr(PQ-PQPQ), equivalent to the squared commutator via ||[P,Q]||_F^2=2 Tr(PQ-PQPQ). Positive spectral-gap coefficient gives equality iff A,B commute; scalar inputs and t endpoints are handled separately. Independent 120 random real two-spectral tests confirm all Ky Fan sums and Frobenius formula, not general proof.
residual_risks: General all-spectrum Bourin inequality remains open and is not asserted. Equality iff commutation holds specifically for the Frobenius defect, not arbitrary unitarily invariant norms.
